### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/sdui-parser`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/sdui-parser/objectui-lockstep.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/sdui-parser/objectui-lockstep.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bdae71e3b7dcc154515bfc7787b8c3f64bbf40a0` — the merge of head `d36a804054a170573b12506d797277d6ecdba05f` into base `29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bdae71e3b7dcc154515bfc7787b8c3f64bbf40a0 && git checkout bdae71e3b7dcc154515bfc7787b8c3f64bbf40a0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a d36a804054a170573b12506d797277d6ecdba05f && git checkout -B drift-repro 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a && git merge --no-ff d36a804054a170573b12506d797277d6ecdba05f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 29c7157af4fed4738b3da14bbfb008496cbd1f6a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The dev's report is `6198386632`, on head `4815bfa99`. The seat review of record follows the patch round. This comment records why the PR does not land as it stands.

1. **Sibling coupling (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 4).** objectui at the console pin `b9814b334` still writes `template: 'full-width'`: `buildDefaultPageSchema` seeds Studio's record-page create. This PR refuses `full-width` at save, so that create would fail with a 422. `PageNodeSchema` also redeclares `template?: string` over the spec type, which the narrowing breaks; that break is to be measured. Step 4 says such a removal "ships together with the sibling fix and the pin bump — or it does not ship". The plan:
   - An objectui PR (`Part of objectstack-ai/objectstack#23610`, no closing keyword) moves the seed to `default` and lets the type follow the spec. The renderer keeps reading `full-width`, because stored rows still render.
   - `.objectui-sha` is held by PR #23709. Once that lands, this PR merges `main` and moves the pin through `scripts/bump-objectui.sh` to a sha that carries the objectui fix.
   - This PR stays draft until both are in.
2. **In scope by ruling item 2's text:** a region whose name repeats a slot its template already filled is not placed, because the console's `findRegion` takes the first match. It is refused in this PR (the dev's out-of-scope finding, measured on the head). On `dashboard`, other repeated names are grid cells and stay accepted.
3. **The dev's open questions:** Q1 is A, the coupled landing above. Q2 is A, region names match case-insensitively as the console's `findRegion` does. Q3 is A, no D2 conversion.

### ① Derived judgments

Judged against ruling 6190536588 (Q1 A · Q2 A · half 1) and the director's executor terms 6189618343.

**Q1 — `isDefault: true` off a bound record page.** RIGHT.
- One reading, one sentence: `misplacedDefaultPageRefusal` (`spec/src/ui/default-record-page.ts`) reuses `defaultRecordPageObject`, so the parse and the registry refuse exactly the pages the record-page rule does not place. `checkPageDefaultPlacement` is attached to `PageSchema` by identifier (pinned in `object-refinement-check-exports.test.ts`), so `definePage`, `defineStack` / `os validate` / `os build` (`STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` 422 at `pages.N.isDefault`) and the save door (`422 INVALID_METADATA`, nothing stored, both kernel topologies) refuse through one parse. The ruling's third door, package registration, is served by `SchemaRegistry.refuseDefaultRecordPageConflicts` → `misplacedDefaultPages` (manifest `pages` and nested `plugins[].pages`, thrown ahead of every mutation and before the `selfId` early return) and by the package-bound `registerItem` seam; `MisplacedDefaultPageError` is `INVALID_METADATA` 422 carrying the parse's sentence — no new code, right. The bare slot (a stored row hydrating with no package) is not judged: right, and consistent with the stored-row paragraph the changeset states.
- The sentence names the app's first navigation item and the APP's own `isDefault`, as item 1 requires (both pinned). A record page with no `object` gets the bind-the-object variant: right — it is a page `defaultRecordPageObject` does not place.
- The showcase's `capability-map.page.ts` drops the flag and stays the landing by navigation order; the three other showcase `isDefault: true` pages (`settings`, `project-detail`, `task-detail`) and platform-objects' `sys_user` / `sys_organization` pages are record pages bound to objects (read on the head) — nothing first-party trips the new refusal.
- D3 entry `page-is-default-off-record-page-refused`, no D2, no grace window: right per item 1.

**Q2 — the closed template set.** RIGHT.
- `PageTemplateSchema` = `default`, `header-sidebar-main`, `three-column`, `dashboard` through `enumWithRetiredValues`; `full-width` is refused BY NAME with the prescription `default` — a retirement, not an alias window. The executor premise held: at the pin `1f23d5b07` objectui `page.tsx:475-476` maps `default` and `full-width` to the same `FullWidthTemplate`, no rendering fork, so nothing was owed on the card.
- `PAGE_TEMPLATE_SLOTS` matches item 2's table exactly (`dashboard` = header / footer plus the open grid, `PAGE_TEMPLATE_OPEN_GRID`). `checkPageRegionPlacement` refuses at `regions.N.name`, naming the slots and a rename (`left_sidebar` → `sidebar`, `right_sidebar` → `aside`, `content` → `main`), on `kind: 'full'` pages only and case-insensitively. The `kind` scoping and the case rule are faithful readings of "a region the chosen template will not place": a `slotted` / `html` / `react` page lays out no region by template, and the renderer's `findRegion` lowercases both sides (`page.tsx:87`). Parse-only (`os validate`, save): item 2 names those two doors and no registry door, so the registry judges Q1 alone. Right by the ruling's text.
- The duplicate-slot refusal added in the patch round (a second `main`; on `dashboard` a second `header` / `footer`): the seat read it into item 2 on the PR (6199121442 #2), and the reading holds — the renderer draws the first region of a name and `getRemainingRegions` excludes that name (`page.tsx:91-94`), so a second one is a region the template will not place. `dashboard`'s other names stay two grid cells: right.
- D3 entry `page-template-closed-region-unplaced-refused`, no D2: right (item 2, no alias window; which slot a renamed region fills is the author's call).
- Consumers inside the diff: `layout-dsl.mdx`'s three `os:check-yaml` pages (`standard` / `console`, `left` / `right`) now spell real templates and slots; `task-visualizations.pages.ts` takes `as const`, and the changeset carries that one-line migration for a `template` held in a widened `string`. Right.

**Half 1.** RIGHT. The `PageTypeSchema` docblock and enum comments say what runs (three widths of one region layout; `home` is not a landing; `utility` has no floating or docked slot); the `utility` print refusal drops "floating panel" and its pin asserts the word is gone; `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx` (types table, a Templates table, the `isDefault` row, `content` → `main`); the four liveness rows re-cited at objectui `0656b0e3c0`; the `utility` value stays (item 3).

**Public surface.** RIGHT. New exports `PageTemplateSchema`, `PageTemplate`, `PAGE_TEMPLATE_SLOTS`, `PAGE_TEMPLATE_OPEN_GRID`, `checkPageDefaultPlacement`, `checkPageRegionPlacement`, `misplacedDefaultPageRefusal` (`@objectstack/spec/ui`) and `MisplacedDefaultPageError` / `MISPLACED_DEFAULT_PAGE_CODE` (`@objectstack/objectql`); `api-surface`, `export-origins`, `declaration-map`, `json-schema.manifest` and `content/docs/references` regenerated and green.
